edges.description: Reflux carries bacteria from the bladder into the renal pelvis and parenchyma. Reflux and sustained kidney infection together, not sterile reflux, produce reflux nephropathy.
Stasis above an obstruction lets uropathogens persist and recur in the upper tract.
Stones keep scarring progressing in adults, in whom scarring otherwise usually stabilizes.
Ascending uropathogenic infection produces tubulointerstitial nephritis and recruits leukocytes into the infected segment.
The predisposing reflux or obstruction persists, so infections recur.
Recurrences reach the kidney as febrile pyelonephritis.
Macrophage-dominated inflammation drives the fibrotic response that leaves a scar.
Activated myofibroblasts deposit the interstitial matrix of the scar.
Scarred segments lose their nephrons, and the surviving glomeruli carry more load.

edges.description: The scarred kidney raises blood pressure; removing it can cure the hypertension.
The scar is seen as focal cortical loss on DMSA and imaging.
Scar contraction over the papilla blunts and dilates the calyx.
Extensive scarring shrinks the whole kidney.
Tubulointerstitial damage impairs urine concentration.
Damaged proximal tubules fail to reabsorb filtered low-molecular-weight proteins.
Remnant-nephron overload is followed by secondary segmental glomerulosclerosis in some kidneys.

evidence.snippet: Microalbuminuria, which is indicative of glomerular damage at a very early stage and precedes overt proteinuria, progressive renal damage and renal failure, has been reported in 51% pediatric patients

nodes.description: After microbiological cure with ceftriaxone, a minority of mice develop renal scars with fibrosis and persistent inflammation, and occasional mice develop chronic kidney disease.

Hypertension and proteinuria are the complications that most affect long-term renal outcome, and both can be treated medically. ACE inhibitors or angiotensin receptor blockers are used for proteinuria. In children with congenital kidney and urinary tract anomalies, which include reflux nephropathy, their benefit is unproven. A 6-12 month trial is suggested, stopping the drug if proteinuria does not improve.
nodes.id: Blood pressure control and RAAS blockade

evidence.reference_title: Vesicoureteral reflux and reflux nephropathy.
evidence.snippet: Of these, hypertension and proteinuria are the commonest ones that have a significant bearing on long-term renal outcome and both are amenable to medical intervention.

evidence.reference_title: Renin angiotensin aldosterone inhibitors in the treatment of proteinuria in children with congenital anomalies of the kidney and urinary tract: more evidence needed.
evidence.snippet: RAASi are effective in reducing proteinuria and slowing CKD progression in many renal conditions; however, the efficacy of these drugs in patients affected by CAKUT with proteinuria is still unknown.

evidence.reference_title: Renin angiotensin aldosterone inhibitors in the treatment of proteinuria in children with congenital anomalies of the kidney and urinary tract: more evidence needed.
evidence.snippet: a 6-12-month trial with RAASi with gradual increase to the maximal tolerated dose should be considered. If no improvement of proteinuria is obtained, the RAASi should be discontinued.

nodes.description: Blunted, dilated calyx beneath the cortical scar. It distinguishes the pyelonephritic scar from an ischaemic one.

evidence.reference_title: The diagnosis of the scars of chronic pvelonephritis.
evidence.snippet: whereas in focal pyelonephritic scars the narrowed parenchyma is associated with clubbing of the calyx in the affected area

nodes.description: 24% of adults with reflux nephropathy had a creatinine clearance below 70 mL/min, more often with severe bilateral disease.

evidence.reference_title: A long term follow up of adults with reflux nephropathy.
evidence.snippet: Seventy-one (24%) had a creatinine clearance < 70 mL/min and 43 (15%) a urinary tract infection.

nodes.description: Daily low-dose trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole in children with reflux after a first or second febrile infection. In the RIVUR trial it halved recurrences but did not reduce renal scarring. It increased trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole resistance in breakthrough E. coli (63% vs 19%). Its use is now selective, with most benefit for high-grade reflux and bladder and bowel dysfunction.

evidence.reference_title: Antimicrobial prophylaxis for children with vesicoureteral reflux.
evidence.snippet: Among children with vesicoureteral reflux after urinary tract infection, antimicrobial prophylaxis was associated with a substantially reduced risk of recurrence but not of renal scarring.

evidence.reference_title: Antimicrobial prophylaxis for children with vesicoureteral reflux.
evidence.snippet: Among 87 children with a first recurrence caused by Escherichia coli, the proportion of isolates that were resistant to trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole was 63% in the prophylaxis group and 19% in the placebo group.

evidence.reference_title: Renal Scarring in the Randomized Intervention for Children with Vesicoureteral Reflux (RIVUR) Trial.
evidence.snippet: Antimicrobial prophylaxis did not decrease the risk of renal scarring.

evidence.reference_title: Vesicoureteral Reflux.
evidence.snippet: patients with grade IV or V reflux, as well as those with combined bladder or bowel dysfunction along with any grade of reflux, received the most benefit from continuous prophylaxis as they have the highest risk.

nodes.description: Patchy interstitial fibrosis, chronic inflammation and tubular atrophy produce a coarse, usually polar cortical scar. The scar overlies a distorted, clubbed calyx and contains thyroidization-type atrophic tubules. Calyceal deformity beneath the scar separates the pyelonephritic scar from an ischaemic one. On CT the scars can mimic lobar infarcts.

animal_models.name: Antibiotic-treated murine pyelonephritis (male C3H/HeN)

evidence.reference_title: Reflux Nephropathy.

evidence.snippet: Chronic pyelonephritis-which appears as focal polar scars with underlying calyceal distortion, global atrophy, and hypertrophy of residual tissue-may mimic at imaging lobar infarcts.

evidence.reference_title: The diagnosis of the scars of chronic pvelonephritis.
evidence.snippet: In 13 of 14 examples in which the evidence pointed to chronic pyelonephritis there was clubbing of the calyx associated with the scar.

evidence.reference_title: Renal scar formation and kidney function following antibiotic-treated murine pyelonephritis.
evidence.snippet: a matching fraction of mice 1 month later exhibited renal scars featuring fibrosis and ongoing inflammatory infiltrates.

nodes.description: Delayed antibiotic treatment of a febrile urinary tract infection has been linked to more renal injury, but a trial found no rise in scarring with delay. The effect is uncertain.
nodes.id: Delayed treatment of febrile urinary tract infection

evidence.reference_title: Vesicoureteral reflux associated renal damage: congenital reflux nephropathy and acquired renal scarring.
evidence.snippet: Specific risk factors for acute pyelonephritis and renal scarring in patients with vesicoureteral reflux include higher reflux grade, dysfunctional voiding/elimination, recurrent pyelonephritic episodes and delayed initiation of antibiotic therapy.

evidence.reference_title: Vesicoureteral reflux and reflux nephropathy.
evidence.snippet: However, the Italian Renal Infection Study Trials reported that the progressive delay in antibiotic treatment of acute pyelonephritis from <1 to > 5 days after the onset of fever was not associated with any significant increase in the risk of scarring on Dimercaptosuccinic acid (DMSA) renal scans obtained 1 year later.

nodes.description: Secondary FSGS was found in 18 of 86 pediatric reflux nephrectomy specimens, was associated with hypertension, and was seen in 27.9% of a hospital chronic pyelonephritis series. Another biopsy series found mostly global sclerosis, with FSGS very rare.

evidence.reference_title: Focal and segmental glomerulosclerosis in children with reflux nephropathy.
evidence.snippet: FSGS was found in 18 patients, 9 of whom were less than 5 years old.

evidence.reference_title: Focal and segmental glomerulosclerosis in children with reflux nephropathy.
evidence.snippet: Within the index population FSGS was significantly (P < .01) associated with hypertension

evidence.reference_title: Renal pathology in patients with reflux nephropathy. The turning point in irreversible renal disease.
evidence.snippet: Among our specimens, most cases of glomerular sclerosis were global while focal segmental glomerulosclerosis was very rare.

nodes.description: HIV infection was a risk factor in 14% of cases in a Nigerian hospital series.

evidence.reference_title: Clinical, morphologic and histological features of chronic pyelonephritis: An 8-year review.
evidence.snippet: Urinary tract obstruction, poorly treated UTI, and HIV infection were major risk factors seen in this environment.

nodes.description: Hypertension is the commonest late complication. It occurred in 38% of 294 adults with reflux nephropathy at last follow-up, more often with severe bilateral scarring. Reported rates are 17-30% in children with scarring and 34-38% in adults. In a Nigerian hospital series of mixed causes it was 16.3%. Malignant hypertension occurs with extensive damage.

evidence.reference_title: A long term follow up of adults with reflux nephropathy.
evidence.snippet: 113 patients (38%) had hypertension or were on antihypertensive therapy. This was significantly more frequent in those with severe bilateral renal parenchymal scarring.

evidence.reference_title: Vesicoureteral reflux and reflux nephropathy.
evidence.snippet: Hypertension occurs in 17%–30% of pediatric patients 32 and 34–38% of adult patients with renal scarring

evidence.reference_title: Long-term effects of reflux nephropathy on blood pressure and renal function in adults.
evidence.snippet: Malignant hypertension developed in 4 patients, all had extensive renal damage.

nodes.description: A urine concentration defect from tubulointerstitial damage.

evidence.reference_title: Vesicoureteral reflux and reflux nephropathy.
evidence.snippet: These include hypertension, proteinuria, urine concentration defects, hyperkalemia, acidosis, and chronic kidney disease with progressive renal failure, including end-stage renal failure (ESRF) in some patients.

nodes.description: Interstitial fibroblasts are activated to myofibroblasts under TGF-beta signalling. An activating TGFB1 promoter allele predicts scarring after childhood urinary tract infection independently of reflux.

biological_processes: transforming growth factor beta receptor signaling pathway

evidence.reference_title: Functional polymorphisms in transforming growth factor-beta-1 (TGFbeta-1) and vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) genes modify risk of renal parenchymal scarring following childhood urinary tract infection.
evidence.snippet: Multiple logistic regression testing identified the presence of VUR (odds ratio 12.4, CI 3.8-40; P < 0.001) and the TGFbeta-1 -509 T allele (OR 6.1, CI 2.4-15.5; P < 0.001) as independent risk factors for renal scarring after UTI.

nodes.description: Increased urinary beta2-microglobulin, retinol-binding protein and other tubular proteins reflect tubular damage.

evidence.reference_title: Vesicoureteral reflux and reflux nephropathy.
evidence.snippet: Patients with RN also spill increased amount of low molecular weight proteins (LMWP) such as beta 2-microglobin (B2M), retinol-binding protein (RBP), alfa 1-microglobin (A1M), and N-acetyl-β-D-glucosaminase (NAG)

nodes.description: Removal of a unilateral poorly functioning or nonfunctioning scarred kidney normalized blood pressure in 6 of 8 hypertensive children with reflux nephropathy. It did not help when the other kidney was also scarred. Nephrectomy is also done for pus-filled, nonfunctioning kidneys.

evidence.reference_title: Nephrectomy for hypertension in pediatric patients with a unilateral poorly functioning kidney: a contemporary cohort.
evidence.snippet: Seven of 11 with MCDK were normotensive postoperatively compared to 6/8 patients with reflux nephropathy, and 1/2 patients with UPJ obstruction.

evidence.reference_title: Nephrectomy for hypertension in pediatric patients with a unilateral poorly functioning kidney: a contemporary cohort.
evidence.snippet: There were 2 patients with contralateral renal scarring, both of which remained hypertensive postoperatively.

evidence.reference_title: Clinical, morphologic and histological features of chronic pyelonephritis: An 8-year review.
evidence.snippet: Nephrectomy was done in 17 (39.5%) of the 43 CPN cases, indications for surgery were pus-filled, non-functioning kidneys.

nodes.description: Loss of nephron mass overloads the surviving glomeruli, which enlarge and sclerose. This produces proteinuria and a progressive fall in GFR, which is steepest with extensive bilateral scarring. Secondary focal segmental glomerulosclerosis is reported in some series but was very rare in another.

nodes.description: In neurogenic bladder, starting clean intermittent catheterization and/or anticholinergics early relieves high-pressure stasis. In observational studies this was associated with less secondary reflux, infection and renal deterioration. The evidence carries a high risk of bias.
nodes.id: Proactive bladder management for neurogenic bladder

evidence.reference_title: Systematic review and meta-analysis to study the outcomes of proactive versus delayed management in children with a congenital neurogenic bladder.
evidence.snippet: Delayed management of NB potentially has 3 times higher risks of secondary VUR, non-febrile UTI, and renal deterioration.

evidence.reference_title: Systematic review and meta-analysis to study the outcomes of proactive versus delayed management in children with a congenital neurogenic bladder.
evidence.snippet: However, the evidence is limited by the high risk of bias due to lack of randomization and standardized reporting in observational studies.

nodes.description: Proteinuria was present in 31% of adults with reflux nephropathy, and in 23.3% of a mixed-cause hospital series. It is the worst prognostic feature.

evidence.reference_title: Clinical, morphologic and histological features of chronic pyelonephritis: An 8-year review.
evidence.snippet: Proteinuria was seen in 10 (23.3%) of the patients, hypertension in 7 (16.3%) and haematuria in 3 (7.0%) of cases.

nodes.description: Repeated febrile infections of the renal pelvis and parenchyma, mostly by uropathogenic E. coli, injure the tubulointerstitium of the refluxing or obstructed segments. This injury is the trigger of the scarring cascade. Whether the host's inflammatory response, rather than bacterial virulence, determines who scars is still open.

evidence.snippet: Eight patients (16%) had nine attacks of acute pyelonephritis and 4/5 of the tested E.coli strains from these patients were P-fimbriated.

nodes.description: Neutrophils and macrophages are recruited into the infected tubulointerstitium in proportion to bacterial burden. The extent of this inflammation, more than the infection itself, predicts the later fibrosis.

evidence.reference_title: Inflammation drives renal scarring in experimental pyelonephritis.
evidence.snippet: The extent of fibrosis correlates most significantly with inflammation at 7 and 28 days postinfection. The recruitment of neutrophils and inflammatory macrophages to infected kidneys is proportional to renal bacterial burden.

nodes.description: The whole kidney is small and atrophic, with hypertrophy of residual tissue.

evidence.reference_title: CT imaging of acute and chronic pyelonephritis: a practical guide for emergency radiologists.
evidence.snippet: Chronic pyelonephritis-which appears as focal polar scars with underlying calyceal distortion, global atrophy, and hypertrophy of residual tissue-may mimic at imaging lobar infarcts.

nodes.description: Focal loss of cortex over a calyx, shown on DMSA scintigraphy or urography. This is the defining lesion. About 15% of children have a scar on follow-up DMSA after a first urinary tract infection.

evidence.reference_title: Risk of renal scarring in children with a first urinary tract infection: a systematic review.
evidence.snippet: 15% (95% CI: 11-18) had evidence of renal scarring on the follow-up DMSA scan.

evidence.reference_title: Clinical, morphologic and histological features of chronic pyelonephritis: An 8-year review.
evidence.snippet: Scarring, reported in 79.0% of patients, was the most common pathological finding, followed by pus casts in 48.8% and focal segmental glomerulosclerosis in 27.9%.

nodes.description: Scarred kidneys raise systemic blood pressure. Removing a small scarred kidney can cure the hypertension. Plasma renin activity does not correlate with blood pressure or with the degree of scarring, so the mechanism is not settled.

biological_processes: regulation of systemic arterial blood pressure

evidence.reference_title: Vesicoureteral reflux and reflux nephropathy.
evidence.snippet: The relationship between renal scarring and hypertension was first demonstrated in 1937 when the removal of a small scarred kidney cured hypertension in a 10 year old female with recurrent UTI and hypertension

evidence.reference_title: Vesicoureteral reflux and reflux nephropathy.
evidence.snippet: The plasma rennin activity (PRA) may increase in some children with renal scars as they grow older, but there is no direct correlation between BP and PRA, plasma creatinine concentration, or degree of scarring

nodes.description: Kidney failure developed in 16 of 115 adults with reflux followed for a median 16 years. Reflux nephropathy accounts for about 5% of pediatric kidney transplants.

evidence.reference_title: Long-term effects of reflux nephropathy on blood pressure and renal function in adults.
evidence.snippet: Sixteen patients developed end-stage renal disease.

evidence.reference_title: Vesicoureteral Reflux.
evidence.snippet: End-stage renal failure in children due to reflux nephropathy accounts for about 5% of all pediatric renal transplants.

nodes.description: Ureteral reimplantation or endoscopic subureteric injection corrects reflux. Trials have not shown surgery to be better than prophylaxis at preventing recurrent infection or scarring. It is generally reserved for high-grade reflux or failure of prophylaxis.
nodes.id: Surgical or endoscopic correction of reflux

evidence.reference_title: Vesicoureteral reflux and reflux nephropathy.
evidence.snippet: Surgical treatment in spite of offering the quickest possible correction of the VUR has not been shown to be superior to antimicrobial prophylaxis as for as recurrence of UTI or renal scarring are concerned.

evidence.reference_title: Vesicoureteral Reflux.
evidence.snippet: endoscopic treatment does not offer significant advantages over antibiotic prophylaxis in preventing new UTIs or renal scarring in most patients.

nodes.description: Obstruction by calculi or strictures, or a high-pressure neurogenic bladder, causes urinary stasis. Stasis predisposes the upper tract to persistent and recurrent infection and to scarring.

evidence.reference_title: Morphologic and urodynamic predictors of renal scarring in pediatric neurogenic bladder A cross-sectional study.
evidence.snippet: Renal scarring was identified in 55.6% of patients.

nodes.description: Incompetent ureterovesical junctions let bladder urine reflux to the renal pelvis. Compound papillae at the renal poles let it pass on into the collecting ducts. Reflux is the structural predisposition, and higher reflux grades carry more risk of scarring.

evidence.reference_title: Risk of renal scarring in children with a first urinary tract infection: a systematic review.
evidence.snippet: Children with vesicoureteral reflux (VUR) were significantly more likely to develop pyelonephritis (relative risk [RR]: 1.5 [95% CI: 1.1-1.9]) and renal scarring (RR: 2.6 [95% CI: 1.7-3.9]) compared with children with no VUR.

evidence.reference_title: Renal Scarring in the Randomized Intervention for Children with Vesicoureteral Reflux (RIVUR) Trial.
evidence.snippet: The proportion of new scars in renal units with grade 4 VUR was significantly higher than in units with no VUR (OR, 24.2; 95% CI, 6.4 to 91.2).
